the use of document surrogates for collection selection is more effective than the use of collection lexicons, and that the conclusions of previous work are not valid when applied to collections that have been created and maintained in a manner similar to how they would be used in a production environment.

collection selection based on document surro gates is more effective for managed collections, and that conclusions drawn from previous artificial collections are not applicable to the managed collections that are likely to exist in the real world.

In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the efficiency of distributed information retrieval systems.
the design and implementation of techniques for collection selection in a distributed document database.
the problem of how to choose collections to be interrogated in a distributed document database, in order to maximize the probability of retrieving the documents that are of interest.

, in the absence of a collection selection index that can be computed quickly and efficiently, the use of a collection ranking index based on document surro- gates is the most promising approach for collection selection.

, for the type of distributed document database that we have studied, collection selection using surrogates is effective, but that there is no single best approach, and that a number of different techniques are worth considering.

, when the collections are managed in a way that is realistic, the use of document surrogates as selection index is more effective than using collection lexicons.
, for the task of collection selection in a managed document database, a simple technique based on document surro- gates is more effective than a more sophisticated method.
the use of a collection selection index is a useful way of improving the performance of distributed document retrieval, but that the choice of selection index is critical to its success.

, in the context of distributed document retrieval, the choice of collections for ranking is critical, and that ranking based on collection lexicon is less effective than ranking based on document content.
